part_title: Hands-On CloudFront OAC Security and Cache Verification

scenes.title: CloudFront private S3 origin (OAC) and bucket policy verification
scenes.narration: This is a guided security lab, so follow its steps in order. Begin with an S3 bucket that is private and protected from public access. Create an Origin Access Control in CloudFront, then attach it to the distribution's S3 origin so requests from CloudFront can be signed appropriately. Next, modify the bucket policy to allow the CloudFront service principal to read the intended objects only when the SourceArn matches the specific distribution. The diagram shows the authorized path from the viewer through CloudFront to the bucket and a direct S3 object request that should be rejected. The expected sample results are HTTP two hundred through the distribution and HTTP four hundred three for direct public access. Do not copy placeholder bucket ARNs or distribution IDs into production. When the test does not match expectations, inspect deployment status, the origin selection, the OAC signing setting, the bucket policy condition and permissions. Remember that restricting S3 origin access does not itself authenticate every viewer at CloudFront.

scenes.title: Lab — Cache verification with CloudFront
scenes.narration: This lab tests the behavior introduced earlier with real repeated requests rather than just a diagram. Begin by uploading a sample index page and versioned JavaScript objects to the S3 origin. Request the page through the CloudFront distribution and inspect response headers such as X-Cache and Age. An initial cache miss can fetch the object from the origin, after which a repeat request may be a hit if it reaches a cache holding the object and the TTL has not expired. The sample output illustrates this pattern but is not a guarantee for each first request or edge location. Next request a separately named version, such as app dot v two dot js, which has a different cache key and may require its own origin fetch. Finally create a CloudFront invalidation for the intended object paths and verify that subsequent requests retrieve refreshed content. Versioned object names often avoid broad invalidations for static assets. Do not cache personalized AI results with a shared cache key.
